@@ -40,5 +40,12 @@
     comparison operators, and its first-vs-last-match behavior — instead of inventing a different or
     paraphrased rule that only happens to fit the one sample you can see (it will diverge on the two
-    hidden files).
+    hidden files). In particular, when the cells you must fill ALREADY contain formulas in the input,
+    those formulas ARE the reference answer — they recalculate correctly on every hidden file. Do NOT
+    overwrite them with literal numbers you computed from this one file: a literal is frozen to the
+    values you happened to see and will be wrong on the other two files, even when it matches here.
+    Leave a correct existing formula in place, or — only if the task asks you to fix or extend it —
+    write a corrected/extended FORMULA, never a hardcoded value. Note that per-cell formulas may
+    differ across the range (e.g. one column references row 2 minus row 3, another row 2 minus row 4);
+    reproduce each cell's own reference pattern rather than forcing one uniform rule over all of them.
 
 PRODUCE THE RESULT, NOT THE RECIPE. Instructions are usually phrased as a request to write a
@@ -56,4 +63,13 @@
 of those, compute the result in Python and write the resulting literal values instead of a formula.
 
+WHEN THE REQUEST IS TO FIND / IDENTIFY / HIGHLIGHT, THE ANSWER CELL STILL WANTS THE VALUE. Some tasks
+ask you to locate or highlight the cell(s) that meet a numeric condition — e.g. "highlight the values
+that sum to X", "find the combination that totals Y", "mark the rows where …", "how many … match".
+The grader compares cell VALUES, not colors/fills, so highlighting or coloring alone leaves the graded
+answer_position cell empty and scores 0. When answer_position is a cell (or small range) that is BLANK
+in the input, write the NUMERIC RESULT of the search into it — the achieved sum, the count, or the
+located value — computed from the data at run time. Do the coloring too if asked, but never finish
+with the answer cell still empty.
+
 MATCH THE EXPECTED CELL'S VALUE AND TYPE. Each answer cell is compared to the expected file by value
 AND by type (numbers compared rounded to 2 decimals; a plain numeric string like "511.7" counts as
@@ -66,4 +82,10 @@
   - Copy text answers verbatim: do not change the letter-casing or wording of a label you read from
     the sheet unless the instruction explicitly asks you to.
+  - When you extract or truncate a string (keep the text before/after a delimiter or keyword, split on
+    a character, take a substring), preserve the surviving characters EXACTLY. Do not `.strip()`,
+    `.rstrip()`, or `.lstrip()` away surrounding spaces, and do not re-case, unless the instruction
+    explicitly says to trim — Excel's LEFT/MID/RIGHT keep those spaces, so trimming them makes your
+    value differ from the expected (e.g. "keep the text before 'FT'" on "abc FT x" must yield "abc ",
+    with the trailing space, not "abc").
   - If the answer cell, or an adjacent already-filled example cell, has a data type and number_format,
     mirror them.
